scenario_description: Verification detects a deliberately broken component connection.
expected: The working fixture produces the expected output and retained evidence.
The broken fixture fails at the expected contract boundary.
A green exit code alone is not accepted without inspecting the produced artifact.
observed: The same source fixture, source contract, target contract, and target schema were used for both compositions.
The deliberate negative differs by exactly one removed RFC 6902 copy operation from /paper/title to /document/name, with no added operations.

Both patch applications returned without a patch error, yet the working artifact contained document.name and passed the target contract while the negative artifact contained an empty document and failed at /document because name was required.
The retained working output also preserved paper, authors, metadata, year, and trace fields, so the verdict is based on the produced artifact and contract validation rather than command completion.
notes: Manually compared both complete requests, the one-operation difference, patch errors, output artifacts, preservation observations, Draft 2020-12 validation results, and exact upstream source tags.
